name: Bistek Tagalog (Filipino Beef and Onions over Rice)
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Five-ingredient braise that gets better held overnight. Filipino beef is missing from the catalog (only pork and chicken are represented). Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated. | HARVEST: Rice is a serving suggestion, not in the source ingredient list.
intro_html: Bistek Tagalog answers the question every budget cook eventually asks: how do you make a little steak feed a lot of people? You slice it thin, soak it in lemon juice, soy sauce, and a serious amount of garlic, then bury it under soft fried onions. Each bowl carries 33 grams of protein and 564 calories for about $2.56. Five real ingredients, one pan, fourteen dinners.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Rice, 6.25 cups dry: ~$1.41. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2lb bags.
Pantry seasonings (black pepper, salt): ~$0.19. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $35.79 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.56 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $40.59 across 14 servings, roughly $2.90 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $13.36 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $53.95. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $2.56 a bowl for steak and rice. The onions do as much work on the plate as the beef does, and onions are the cheapest thing in the produce aisle.
shop_smart: The flank or sirloin is the entire budget here. Buy it when the case gets marked down and freeze it flat. You are slicing it thin anyway, and a half frozen steak slices a lot cleaner than a room temperature one.
Bottled lemon juice is the right call. Calamansi is the traditional citrus and it is nearly impossible to find in Omaha, so ReaLemon is the honest stand in and it keeps in the fridge door for months.
Garlic goes in by the handful in this dish. Buy whole heads instead of the peeled jars. Heads keep for weeks in a dry bowl and cost far less per clove.
Yellow onions are a main ingredient, not a garnish. Grab the mesh bag instead of loose singles, because the per pound price is almost always lower.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the beef thin against the grain. Toss it with the lemon juice, soy sauce, minced garlic, and black pepper, then let it sit at least 30 minutes while you prep everything else.
Slice the onions into rings. Fry them in a little of the oil over medium heat until soft and just starting to brown, then pull them out and set them aside.
Lift the beef out of the marinade and save every drop of that liquid. Sear the beef in batches over high heat so it browns instead of steaming.
Return all the beef to the pot, pour in the reserved marinade and a splash of water, and bring it to a simmer.
Cover and simmer gently for 25 to 30 minutes, until the beef is tender and the sauce has thickened into a glaze.
Cook the rice separately while the beef simmers.
Stir the fried onions back in for the last 2 minutes, taste, and add salt only if the soy sauce did not carry it far enough.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Scoop that weight of beef and onions into each container, then add the same weight of rice to every one. Every bowl lands at 564 calories with 33 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from gypsyplate.com, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.

head.description: Filipino Bistek Tagalog meal prep: thin steak braised in lemon, soy, and garlic under soft fried onions, served over rice. 564 calories, 33g protein, about $2.56 per serving.
head.keywords: bistek tagalog, filipino beef, beef and onions, budget meal prep, steak rice bowls, filipino meal prep
recipeIngredient: 3.5 lb beef flank or sirloin steak
steps: Slice the beef thin and marinate it in lemon juice, soy sauce, garlic, and pepper.
Fry the onion rings in oil until soft, then set them aside.
Sear the drained beef in batches over high heat.
Add the reserved marinade and a splash of water, then simmer covered 25 to 30 minutes.
Stir the onions back in, cook the rice, and portion into 14 containers.
